There are cases, and I'm not suggesting it has happened here, that witnesses elaborate their stories; they tell one version to the Prosecution's investigator, they tell another story to the MUP, and then they come along here in court and tell a third story. That's very relevant to know what weight should be given to that witness's evidence. I repeat: I'm not suggesting that's what happened here. But the Defence counsel is entitled to ask whether you have given any other statements to anybody else. Now, you've given one to the Prosecution. Did you give one to anybody else: That's the question. Is there some problem that you have with answering that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I did make a statement in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And is there some problem in telling us to whom you made that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: No, there's no problem, because it is a man who, on his own initiative, investigated the suffering of Bosniaks in Visegrad municipality. He took it down in an ordinary book and he interviewed people about what they had experienced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, that man has died. His name was Mesanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understood your last answer properly, you made a statement to this gentleman, Mr. Mesanovic, who was writing a book, but you didn't give any statements to the MUP authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I don't remember at all that any MUP institutions took any statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would probably remember if you had been interviewed by anyone from the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina or that you had signed such a statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I did not give a statement in the MUP, but there were commissions for the investigation of war crimes against Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mention the name of Mitar Vasiljevic in your earlier statements, including your statement to this gentleman Mesanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: To Mesanovic I did not, but about Mitar, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, if Mesanovic is the only one you gave statements to apart from the investigator of this Tribunal, if you say that you didn't talk about Mitar Vasiljevic to him, then to whom did you speak about Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I have already told you that there was a commission for the investigation of war crimes - that was the name of the commission - for the area of Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to ask you again: Did you give them any statement regarding the incidents in Visegrad during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I have to tell you now that [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I asked about you, yourself, personally. Did you make any statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me now ask you a few questions about this statement of yours, which I assume you remember, because it was in January this year. I looked through it carefully after your testimony today, and in the statement I did not find anywhere you mention seeing the group from Koritnik on the 14th of June. Is it true that in your statement you did not mention that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: Let me tell you: At the time, I was giving a statement only about victim number 13 and the condition she was in and how I saw her, but I'm now telling what I saw in the morning that they went by, and Igbala Kurspahic from Kosovo Polje joined them, and who, with the villagers from Koritnik, was burnt in the same house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I have listened to your testimony today. Do you agree with me that you did not mention that particular fact in the statement that you gave to the investigator of The Hague Prosecution office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: If it is not mentioned in the statement, then it means that I did not state it in the statement. However, I repeat once again that I saw them coming from the direction of Sase towards Visegrad, a group of 50 or 60 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us today that VG13 had told you about the persons who took part in the fire, and you said, first of all, if not only, Mitar Vasiljevic. That is not contained in your statement to the investigator of the Tribunal, that the witness VG13 had indeed told you that. Do you agree with me that that is not mentioned in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I don't know what is written in this January statement, but I wish to state before this Honourable Chamber that the victim number 13 mentioned Milan Lukic, Mitar Vasiljevic, and Bosko Djuric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, madam. You have stated that today. However, you did not mention that particular fact in the statement given to the investigator. Do you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: Right now I cannot even remember what is written in there, but it probably -- the victim number 13 will tell you about her experiences. I'm just telling you what I heard, but I did not see when it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also in your statement, when you spoke about Rasim Torohan, you said that he was going towards Visegrad in the statement to the investigator. Today you testified that he was going in the opposite direction, that is, towards Sase. Do you remember having declared that to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I don't know whether you've had an opportunity to be in the area of Visegrad since 1992, and if you experience death occurring before your very eyes, sometimes it seems to you that he's going towards the town, sometimes in the opposite direction, sometimes towards the woods, in order to save his life. I know that he was pushed into the car and that he was taken in the direction of Visegrad, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct in understanding you that, because of what you have just stated, you cannot be sure as to the direction he was going to? Because if we take into account your fear at the time and the overall situation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: Once again I have to tell you: If you're witnessing death before your very eyes... The man had just lost his glasses. He was thrown into the car. He was going towards Visegrad. And it's so difficult, because all these images, maybe a dozen of them, are happening at the same time before your very eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, madam. I can really understand that. But does it mean that in view of the fact that you have given two different statements concerning the event, that you cannot be sure whether he was going towards Visegrad or in the opposite direction, that is, towards Sase? Can I interpret your answer in that way, for the reasons that you have just indicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: Since his house was close by, in my opinion, he was trying to find shelter in Kosovo Polje, so he was going towards Kosovo Polje. He was walking in the direction of Kosovo Polje at the moment it happened. He was probably turning around, looking for help, asking for help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, he was on the road, he was walking along the road, so I don't see how you can say that he was trying to find shelter. He was on the road. In the statement given to the investigator, you stated that he was walking towards Visegrad. Today you have stated something different. I want to know whether you could clearly see that, whether you could clearly see that once when he was pushed into the car, where he was taken to, in which direction, towards Visegrad or the other one, or if you cannot tell us that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: For me, the most important is the way in which he was taken away and the fact that Professor Torohan has never come back, has never been seen since then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you haven't answered my question. If you wish to answer my question, you can at least tell me whether you remember that that is what you stated to the investigator, that he was walking toward Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: Well, if that's what's stated there, then it means that that is what I stated. But try to put yourself in my shoes. Would you really be turning around and looking at death happening before your very eyes?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but in that case you can tell us that you don't know, if those were the reasons that you didn't see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, look, I really think that we've spent enough time on this. The statement will speak for itself, and the importance of this particular matter is so minute, it's not worth this sort of pressure. Is there anything further you want to ask her?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree, Your Honour. The same event is described in the statement to the effect that the witness was in a cornfield in Kosovo Polje. That is in the statement that she gave to the investigator. Today she told us that she was in the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know whether that exists in your field, and is it true, Witness, that you were in the cornfield on the 18th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: Well, I'm really sorry that the fall is nearing its end, but -- so I'm not able to take you there. There was a cornfield in Kosovo Polje, the Black Locust Wood, also and everything the way I described it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you told the investigator that you had been in a cornfield on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: Counsel, the cornfield is next to the Acacia wood. It is linked, it is connected with that piece of land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And just one more question, Your Honour. In your statement, madam, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [redacted]. What is the name of that place and where exactly was that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I don't know whether you have been in Rujiste in [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: [redacted], and all other villages in the municipality of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was only interested about his house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I know where it is. I know where he was born, I know exactly where his new house in town is. I know everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: Well, you go down the hill, you pass through the meadow, and you get to his grandmother's house, and there's a very old house next to it, and it's the adjacent house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm sorry, just one more question about an event which was not described in the statement, that is, the event which took place on the third day of Kurban -- I'm sorry. On the eve of Kurban Bajram, the day before. You said that Mitar was singing something about the meat that is customarily eaten on the Muslim holiday. You did not describe that event in your statement. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: Sir, if I had spoken about everything that I know and everything that I saw, the Tribunal wouldn't be finished with me for three days. On the 10th of June, 1992, all of the residents of Kosovo Polje were able to see, to observe, because they were all herded in one group. They could see Mitar Vasiljevic in Gajic, standing -- driving -- on the left of the driver, in the passenger's seat, carrying a black flag with skull and bones on it --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I am not asking you about that. You have spoken about that during your testimony today. I just wanted to know whether that incident was described in your statement given to the investigator, because I was unable to find that particular event. That is all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I wish to finish my sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please answer my question, madam?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You are being asked whether you had described that incident to the investigator. You've already told us about the incident here. You are being asked, however, whether you told the investigator about it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: I don't know whether I did. I should have done it, if I didn't, but it did happen on the 10th. Mitar was calling out Muslims, telling them that the next day the Kurban traditional meat would be distributed, and that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome. Re-examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 81, there's been quite a bit of testimony now about Stanko Pecikoza. Can you tell us what his ethnicity was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he a Serbian -- was he a Serb that helped Muslims during this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG81
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted], a very kind and good person, like everybody else from the Pecikoza family. Stanko Pecikoza was one of the wealthiest Serbs in the municipality of Visegrad. He was initially the president of the SDS. I don't know what happened to him later on, what kind of function he had, but there was a disagreement of some sort amongst them. But Stanko Pecikoza helped a lot the Muslim residents of Visegrad. He enabled them to leave the town and go to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think I should say this, Mr. Domazet. There was absolutely no suggestion to her that she had got the date of his death wrong. Now, I hope that we're not going to be faced with a situation that you come along later to prove that she was wrong. You've got to give her the opportunity to explain anything you want to put in opposition to her evidence. Now, you had better come clean, as it were, as to the point you're going to make about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if Your Honour wishes me to do so, but concerning the death of Stanko Pecikoza is indeed -- the date of the death of Stanko Pecikoza is indeed different from what the witness has indicated. Does Your Honour wish me to explore the matter further on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you've got to give her the opportunity to explain whether she may have been in error. That's the whole point of a fair cross-examination. If you don't do it now, it means we may have to bring her back for the Prosecution in a case in reply. There's a rule which actually specifically requires counsel to do this now. It used to be just thought to be an obligation of fairness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. According to what I was able to learn while investigating the case, and I have some documentary evidence about that, Stanko Pecikoza was killed on the 20th of June. At the time, nobody knew about that. The matter became known on the 21st, and he was buried on the 22nd. So that is the information that I was able to obtain. We can put it to the witness, that is, that it was on the 20th of June that Stanko Pecikoza was killed, but that his family was unaware of that fact on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But let's assume it's one day out. What does it matter? The importance of this evidence is that she says that she saw your client, and that's the whole point of it. Now, both of them are after the 14th of June and that's the only relevance of the evidence. That, if I may say so, would not destroy the credit to be given to her evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree with you, Your Honour. You know the reason why those dates are very important for me, and it is important for me that the witness has spoken about the dates of the crossing over and the dates of the events that took place before that, and she said that she crossed the river on the 19th, and she linked several other dates to that particular date, and that's why it was important to me, because she linked it with the date when she learnt about the death of Stanko Pecikoza and when his family said that they could no longer expect their protection. So those were the reasons for my questions concerning this particular matter, and the Defence will call evidence as to the whereabouts of Mitar Vasiljevic at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that's a very different matter, but from the point of view of putting it to the witness, I don't think there's any need Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to do it unless Mr. Groome has some other idea, because the point that she made was that it was after the 14th of June, after she had spoken to -- she had tended this woman whose pseudonym I've forgotten but who had been injured in the fire. So that -- as long as it's after the 14th, that's the point of her evidence, really. A day in, a day out would not make any difference. But you can certainly pursue it later on. Mr. Groome, would you agree that there's no point in putting that to her in cross-examination? She might have been a day out?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, I would, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then, there's no need for you to put it, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm not going to pursue the matter any further, of course, but I should like to ask Mr. Groome for his agreement, that is, that what I have just indicated is not contained in the statement given to the investigator, so that we do not need to tender the entire statement into evidence. If necessary, I can perhaps repeat the relevant points, the inconsistencies, that is. Do you wish me to repeat the inconsistencies?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is a matter that, if it's not easily worked out between you in court, could be worked out after. The witness doesn't have to be here, we can get on to the next witness. That's what I'm concerned about. Perhaps could you speak to Mr. Groome about it later and there will be an agreement, if necessary, by checking it against the transcript and the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means, if it is agreeable to Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, madam, that completes your task here. Thank you very much for coming here to give your evidence and for the evidence you've given. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I just repeat something, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm a little concerned about what it is going to be. What do you want to say? What's the subject matter of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, I have to state that the late Stanko Pecikoza was killed around 6.00 a.m. on the 19th of June, and throughout that day people were coming to express condolences to his family. People were crying. His brother Mlado came to the village and he said that, in addition to what Mr. Stanimir Pecikoza told us, what he told us, the allegations of the Defence are not true. The late Stanko Pecikoza was killed on the 19th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. The Prosecution will no doubt follow that up with you, but you are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Bauer, we won't be sitting after lunch-time today but I think it's worth getting the witness under way.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, Your Honour. The Prosecution calls Witness VG78.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, madam, will you please make the solemn declaration in the document that the Court usher is handing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Could the pseudonym sheet marked 87 please be given to the witness and to the Court. Examined by Ms. Bauer:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness VG78, please -- good afternoon. Relax, sit back.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to conceal your identity, you have been given the pseudonym VG78. I just want you to look at the sheet of paper and state with yes or no whether it contains your name, your date of birth, and the place where you were born.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: VG78, can you please describe to the Court your educational background.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Secondary school. I graduated from secondary school for textile workers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to primary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a moment. The pseudonym sheet will be Exhibit P78 and it is under seal. I'm sorry, Ms. Bauer, but it's better to get them in while we think of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to primary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: I went to primary school in Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your secondary school you were just talking about, where was that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: In Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That should be P87, not 78. I'm sorry. Perhaps I'm developing dyslexia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in 1992 live with your family in the village of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at this sheet and just state with yes or no whether VG101 is your sister.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time in June 1992 when a Serb neighbour called Radomir Djuric came to your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: The 13th of June he came, and he told us to move out on the 14th, in the morning, at 6.00 a.m., that a bus would be waiting for us in Koritnik, the village, in the village where Serbs lived. That is where the bus station was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you why you had to leave the village that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: He said that our neighbours don't dare protect us any more if some other people come, and that is why we left on the 14th of June. We left the village of Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer on the 14th of June with "we," do you refer only to your family or do you refer to more people from the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: The whole village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including the Serb population of the village or only the Muslim population of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: The Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you estimate for the Court, please, how many people, approximately, were in this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: About 50 of us, and then from other settlements, two families joined us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: VG78, we'll come to that point in time. Did you find that the bus station -- was there a bus waiting for you the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your neighbour there the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you decide to go on to the neighbouring village, Greben, to wait for a bus there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the bus come in that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told that the bus broke down and you ought better to go to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes, that is what we were told.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said a moment ago you were joined by more people from other villages. Can you recall which villages those villages were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: The village of Sase and Banja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people do you estimate joined your group from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: I think two families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many people would that be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Seven. Seven members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time did you approximately arrive in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: About 12.15, when the buses had left. So we didn't arrive in time to catch the buses who left at 12.00, that is, the convoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go when you went to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: We went in front of the hotel, along the Drina, and we stood there, and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who, apart from your group, was there at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic was there and those people who were collaborating with him. They were looking after the people who were to join the convoy and those who missed the convoy, to put them up for the night, and so they accompanied us --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to stop you there. Before you go on, you just mentioned a person called Mitar Vasiljevic. I would like to know how you know Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: I knew him by sight. He worked in Visegrad as a waiter. I would see him several times in the bus. The bus would stop at Greben and then drive on to Prelovo, carrying passengers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would Mitar Vasiljevic be a passenger or the driver of the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: A passenger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about his wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: I just know that she worked at Banja, in a shop. I knew her by sight. I would see her there. I would go into the shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when an OTP investigator showed you a colour photo spread?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were shown by an OTP investigator, a representative from the OTP, 12 different pictures of men on one sheet of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would like to go into a short private session. The photo spread is already in evidence under seal, P55-78.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It has a signature on it, does it?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go into private session, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: VG78, would you be able today to recognise the person you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please take a look around in the courtroom and describe where the person sits and what he is wearing, without, please, standing up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: He's sitting in the last row, next to the wall. He has a greyish suit. I can't see very well from here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: May the record --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you maybe --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: And he's got headphones on his head.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Could the record reflect that the witness identified the accused, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the colour of the suit is not quite right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But he's the only one in the back row that is wearing a suit. The security guard is wearing a shirt. I think we can agree, can't we, Mr. Domazet? Yes, she pointed to the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see well from here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Don't worry, Witness 78.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw this person, Mitar Vasiljevic, there at the hotel for the first time, what did you see him doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Well, he was telling us where we should go for the night, because the buses had left for Kladanj, and they said that we should go to Mahala, to spend the night wherever we wanted in those houses, and he went with us with another two or three persons whom I didn't know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you stop for a moment, please. You said he was telling you to go spend the night in some houses. What was Mitar Vasiljevic wearing that day? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: I remember he had a greyish coat and a hat on his head and a uniform underneath the coat, and he had a rifle on his shoulder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything covering his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Mitar Vasiljevic at the hotel, how far away were you from him at that time? Maybe you want to look towards the Judges and say was it closer than the Judges, further away than the Judges, or about the distance from the Judges?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: About ten steps away. When he walked up to slap a person, she said something and he went up to her and slapped her, and then he moved away. He was walking around in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said he told you to go to a certain settlement in Nova Mahala -- in Mahala, sorry. Is Pionirska Street --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- part of Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that he accompanied you. Was he --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- alone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No. There were two or three others. I knew them by sight but not by name, so I didn't really know who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mitar Vasiljevic dressed in the same clothes that you just saw him at the hotel, Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he still armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything disguising his face at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where would he walk? Would he walk right beside you or in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Beside us and in front of us. He was accompanying the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was a column. Was it a column by lines or individuals? What was the column like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: In line, one behind the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was VG101 at that time with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have touched Mitar Vasiljevic from where you were walking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a point in time that you stopped on Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: We stopped when we reached the settlement in front of the houses, and then we entered those houses and that is where we put up, in two houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you to enter those houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you to enter these houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic said, "Go in there. You will spend the night there." He said it, and the men with him, and we got in and settled down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In reference to the school on Pionirska Street, approximately, did you pass the whole school or did you just see the school? Was it across the school? Where were those houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: We passed by the school, and those houses were left of the school, to the left of the school. Jusuf Memic's house was the one we were in, and the other house, the surname was Delija, the family name. So we were in those two houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The larger group was in which house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: In Jusuf Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay throughout the time on the ground floor of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many rooms were in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Two rooms, a kitchen and a corridor. And there was an attic, but there was no one up there. We were just in those two rooms and in the kitchen and in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you give your best estimate; how much time would you say elapsed from when you came from the hotel to the place where -- to the house where you stayed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: I think about 45 minutes, something like that. We spent a little time down there, then we moved over. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic, did he stay with you or did he leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: First he went into the house and took out three persons, and then he brought them back, after about an hour, not even that. And after that, I didn't see him in the house, but one person said Mitar Vasiljevic is calling people to come out to give some kind of a certificate, and that if anyone were to come, he should be told, and that no one must bother us, and that we would be the first to leave by bus to Kladanj. And then I saw these people coming into the house and taking this note.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we please stop there for a moment. Who told you that Mitar Vasiljevic issued a safety passage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: A person from my village, a woman who was with us, and she said that he was calling out a person to go out. She didn't go, but this other person went. And then they got this note for safe passage, that we would be the first to go in the morning to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she tell you to whom he might have given this card?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who he gave it to. I know that people went out and brought back this certificate, this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this certificate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know a certain Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you know him from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted]. So that is how I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time that afternoon that Milan Lukic arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much later was this in relation to the last time you saw Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: About an hour later, maybe less. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it still light outside or already dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: It was light.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic request you to take -- to give away all your valuables, including money, gold, and watches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did everybody have to give away whatever they had on themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a watch at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anybody else at that time, apart from Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do, apart from taking your valuables?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: He came to the door and said, "Give us money and gold. If we find any on anyone, we will cut your throat and cut off your fingers." And he took out a young girl from the village of Musici, and he took her away and I didn't see her again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this woman previously said to have been raped by Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: These Perhaps were not terribly much at issue, Ms. Bauer, but there's been a series of leading questions over the last page. May I suggest you let the witness give the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Milan Lukic left, did there come a time when a group of men came back later that evening? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were these men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: They were the same ones who were there during the daytime. They told us to get out of this house, to go to another one. They wanted to search our things, allegedly to see if there were any weapons. And that is how we came out, one by one, and crossing from one house to the other. With VG101, I managed to escape, to run away, and so I didn't stay there any longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When those men arrived, were they outside or inside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: No. In front of the door they were. They were between the two houses, watching the people as they were moving into the other house. One was in front of the house, with a rifle. He had a moustache. I don't remember his name. I just noticed his face as I was leaving this house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: I saw Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic walking between the two houses. They were not in front of this house which I was leaving, but over there next to the other house. But I ran away, together with VG101. I hid behind the shed and then went down to a creek and through the woods, as far away as I could from the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mitar Vasiljevic wear at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: What he wore in front of the hotel: this coat and a hat. I just saw him for a moment, his profile, in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was dark. Was there any lights outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: There was. There was a light and you could see everything; it was lit up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you stand when you saw Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: I was standing at the edge of the shed. I was about to leave, and I cast a glance that way. I heard the grass moving, and together with VG101, I followed her, and that is how we managed to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you turned around to take a glance, what did the person Mitar Vasiljevic do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: He was walking around with those men of his. They were supervising the people moving. He was looking more towards that house than towards this one where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you say "this one" and "that one," you mean -- which house do you mean? He stood closer to the house you were let out or closer to the other house where you were supposed to be let in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78
utterances.text: Closer to the house that we were supposed to be let into, not over here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: I would ask to go into another private session for introduction of a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think it would be preferable if we took a break now and you can do that on Monday. We will resume at 9.30 on Monday. We will now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st day of October, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 23 24 25
